$comment: SOLUTION DATA payload schemas, one per claim family. Closed schemas (additionalProperties: false) so the answer generator never sees fields outside the family's claim. Times and distances are in published Solomon units (the solver's scaled units divided by SCALING_FACTOR=10). Identifying metadata (instance_id, perturbation_id, action_name) lives in the prompt's CONTEXT block, not the payload, so the generator cannot accidentally re-state context as evidence.

OBJ.title: OBJ payload — objective value and delta vs baseline

objective.description: Constant tag so the generator names the unit. Solomon distance = total route length in the published unit system (solver's int distance / SCALING_FACTOR=10).

action_objective.description: EvaluatedVRPTW.objective from the action that ran, divided by SCALING_FACTOR and rounded to 2 decimals. This is the number the operational-validity check compares against (within 0.5%).

baseline_objective.description: Pre-perturbation objective for the same instance, sourced from Stage A's baseline_obj column (already in unscaled / published units, rounded to 2 decimals). Lets the generator answer 'how much did distance change' without doing arithmetic in tokens.

objective_delta_absolute.description: action_objective - baseline_objective, rounded to 2 decimals. Precomputed so the generator does not compute it inline.

objective_delta_percent.description: 100 * (action_objective - baseline_objective) / baseline_objective, rounded to 2 decimals. Same rationale as delta_absolute.

PV.title: PV payload — plan validity (feasibility) and the reason it fails

feasible.description: EvaluatedVRPTW.feasible. This is the bit the operational-validity check matches against.

capacity_ok.description: EvaluatedVRPTW.feasible_capacity_only — would the routes be capacity-feasible ignoring TW.

time_windows_ok.description: EvaluatedVRPTW.feasible_tw_only — would the routes be TW-feasible ignoring capacity.

coverage_ok.description: EvaluatedVRPTW.is_complete — every instance customer is served.

feasibility_breakdown.description: Three booleans the generator can cite when asked 'why is the plan infeasible'.

infeasibility_kind.description: Output of vrp_copilot_bench.vrptw.evaluation.infeasibility_kind(ev). Encodes the same information as feasibility_breakdown but in the categorical label Stage A uses, so the generator can phrase the answer in either form.

n_unserved_customers.description: Length of EvaluatedVRPTW.unserved_customers. Headline number for coverage-failure questions.

unserved_customer_ids.description: EvaluatedVRPTW.unserved_customers verbatim. Empty list when coverage_ok=true. Lets the generator list IDs without inventing them.

STRUCT.title: STRUCT payload — route count and per-route customer sequence

n_routes.description: len(EvaluatedVRPTW.routes) — count of non-empty routes. Headline number for route-count questions; the operational-validity check compares this for exact equality.

routes.description: EvaluatedVRPTW.routes as a list of route descriptors. Order is the solver's route enumeration order (route_idx). Customer IDs are integers in visit order. Supplies both the 'how many routes' answer (via length) and the 'which route serves customer X' / 'are A and B on the same route' answers (via lookup).

route_idx.description: RouteSummary.route_idx. Stable across the action's other outputs (matches keys in route_costs and route_summaries).

customer_ids.description: Customer IDs visited on this route, in order. Depot (0) is not included.

SCHEDULE.title: SCHEDULE payload — per-customer timing and route-end times

time.description: Constant tag. All time fields are PyVRP's scaled values divided by SCALING_FACTOR=10, rounded to 1 decimal — i.e., Solomon-native minutes.

n_late_customers.description: Sum of RouteSummary.n_late_customers over routes (= EvaluatedVRPTW.n_late_customers). Headline number for 'how many customers are late'.

late_customer_ids.description: Customer IDs for which VisitSchedule.time_warp > 0. Precomputed here because PyVRP does not emit a 'late_customers_list' directly — see rationale doc.

route_end_times.description: One entry per route, projected from RouteSummary. Supports 'what time does route X finish' questions and route-end-disruption claims.

end_time.description: RouteSummary.end_time / SCALING_FACTOR, rounded to 1 decimal (Solomon minutes).

has_time_warp.description: RouteSummary.has_time_warp — whether this route violates any time window.

customer_schedule.description: Full per-customer schedule projected from EvaluatedVRPTW.per_customer_schedule. Included in entirety (one entry per served customer) so the generator can answer questions about any specific customer without inventing IDs. ORDER_CHANGE customers that the action failed to serve do not appear here; they are not addressable for SCHEDULE claims under this action.

start_service.description: VisitSchedule.start_service / SCALING_FACTOR, rounded to 1 decimal. The op-validity check (within 1 minute) is over this field.

tw_early.description: VisitSchedule.tw_early / SCALING_FACTOR. Lets the generator say 'before the window opens at T' truthfully.

tw_late.description: VisitSchedule.tw_late / SCALING_FACTOR. Lets the generator say 'window closed at T'.

is_late.description: True iff VisitSchedule.time_warp > 0. Derived; not in raw PyVRP output.

lateness_minutes.description: VisitSchedule.time_warp / SCALING_FACTOR, rounded to 1 decimal. Zero when on time.
